plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks crowned with huge golden faces that swivel across the sky, turning late-summer fields in the American Midwest into seas of glowing yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Great Plains and Midwest, United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day, then reset overnight. Mature blooms stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Wiry, evergreen shrubs that drape Scottish moors and upland heaths in rolling waves of pink and purple. Thousands of tiny bell-shaped blooms hum with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (about August to October)
plants.location: Moorlands of Scotland and northern Britain
plants.funFact: Heather honey is a prized specialty. The nectar is so thick and gel-like that it can't be spun out of the comb in the usual way.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small Australian tree that bursts into fluffy golden pom-pom flowers. They light up the late-winter bush and fill the air with a honeyed scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (about July to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria and South Australia
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
